text:
alex: Quick heads-up — hit a deploy race this morning. PR merged, ArgoCD picked up new k8s manifests that depend on infra changes, but Terraform (Atlantis) apply finished a bit later. result: crashloops for a few replicas until tf applied. anyone seen this pattern before?

maria: ugh. do you have the PR link and which svc? could be ordering between merge and apply hooks.

alex: PR is https://github.com/redwoodinc/infrastructure/pull/462 — it's a small rds subnet change + a k8s configmap bump in infra-manifests. GH Actions tests passed, merge job merges main, ArgoCD watches main so it synced immediately. Atlantis apply ran as a separate CI job and applied ~30s later.

chris: yes — we saw similar once. Argo will happily sync whatever is in Git. if the git merge happens before the infra is applied upstream, you get dangling references.

noa: quick options: 1) make GH merge job wait for a successful Atlantis apply status before completing the merge (merge gate), 2) have Atlantis call ArgoCD to trigger sync only after apply, or 3) add short health probes/retries in the k8s manifests for dependent services.

alex: thinking 1 or 2 are best. how hard is it to have Atlantis mark a commit status/check? can GH Actions poll a status?

maria: Atlantis can post GitHub checks or statuses if configured (we have a small helper in infra-tools). alternatively easiest: add a GH Actions post-merge step that polls for an "atlantis/apply" success status on the merge commit before finishing. super small script does it.

ci-bot: snippet from infra-tools we use: 
```
# wait-for-atlantis.sh
REPO_OWNER=redwoodinc
REPO=infra
COMMIT_SHA=${GITHUB_SHA}
until gh api repos/$REPO_OWNER/$REPO/commits/$COMMIT_SHA/status --jq '.statuses | map(select(.context=="atlantis/apply" and .state=="success")) | length' | grep -q "1"; do
  echo "waiting for atlantis apply..."
  sleep 10
done
```

chris: or flip it: let Atlantis call ArgoCD (we have a lightweight webhook in ops) so only after terraform finishes it posts to ArgoCD to sync the specific app. advantage: no polling and explicit ordering.

noa: tradeoffs: polling is simple and keeps responsibilities in GH Actions; webhooks require Atlantis to have argocd creds (we can scope them). also think about fallback if Atlantis fails — we should block merge or auto-revert manifests that require infra.

alex: cool. i'll prototype the GH Actions poll step first (less infra changes). will open a PR and ping here. thanks all. :thumbsup:

maria: nice — cc @chris if you want to try the webhook version later.

chris: happy to help with argocd webhook. we also should add a short doc in eng-infra/wiki about this pattern so future PRs don't regress.

alex: agreed — i'll add a one-pager with the recommended patterns and the wait script.

ci-bot: filed task INFRA-981 to track docs + merge-gate implementation.
